objective: Configure service discovery and load balancing across clusters with Cluster Mesh: cilium clustermesh enable and connect, global services, and affinity annotations
secondaryObjectives: Understand the benefits of Cluster Mesh for multi-cluster connectivity: Pod IP routing across clusters, shared identities and policy, and high availability

sources.cite: Isovalent, 'The New CNCF Cilium Certified Associate (CCA) Certification!'
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the certification body's page, found by WebSearch. Confirms the exam domains and weights: Architecture 20%, Network Policy 18%, Service Mesh 16%, Network Observability 10%, Installation and Configuration 10%, Cluster Mesh 10%, eBPF 10%, BGP and External Networking 6%. The objective wording is the course seed's.

sources.cite: Cilium documentation, Setting up Cluster Mesh (latest)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: each cluster needs a unique name and a unique numeric ID from 1 to 255; PodCIDR ranges in all clusters must not conflict; changing the ID or name of a cluster with running workloads requires restarting them, because the ID is part of security identities; cilium clustermesh enable in each cluster, then cilium clustermesh connect once.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: a global service is a Service with identical name and namespace in each cluster, each annotated service.cilium.io/global: "true"; Cilium then load-balances to Pods in both clusters.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: service.cilium.io/affinity: local load-balances across healthy local backends and uses remote ones only when no local backend is available or healthy; none is the default.

The company, the clusters, the services and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Pellmark Retail, a fictional store chain. The checkout service runs in two clusters, east and west. Last month an east outage took checkout down for an hour; the plan is Cluster Mesh so each cluster can fail over to the other's checkout Pods.
handover: Both clusters were built from the same Terraform module: cluster name 'default', cluster ID 0, Pod CIDR 10.0.0.0/16.
Checkout's database writes are fastest from the local cluster.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: colliding identities make east's policies match west's Pods; some payment traffic is dropped and some unexpected traffic allowed.
Check-in 3: east's checkout Pods crash on a bad node pool; checkout is down for 40 minutes while DNS is switched and caches expire.
Check-in 4: east's Pods restart under load; with west no longer shared, east's checkout fails for 10 minutes.

effects.log: Check-in 1: the mesh can't be connected as things are.
Check-in 2: the mesh is up; checkout still only sees local Pods.
Check-in 3: half of checkout calls now cross to the other region.

idsPrompt.title: Same name, same ID, same CIDR
idsPrompt.context: The clusters collide on name, ID and Pod CIDR. West is new and carries no production traffic yet; east is live.

choices.label: Rebuild the empty west cluster with name west, ID 2 and Pod CIDR 10.8.0.0/16, give east name east and ID 1 in a planned agent rollout, then cilium clustermesh enable and connect

effects.log: Unique names, IDs and CIDRs; the clusters connect.

choices.feedback: Unique names and IDs keep identities apart, and non-overlapping Pod CIDRs let Pod IPs route between clusters.

choices.label: Change the names and IDs but keep the shared Pod CIDR and route through gateways later

effects.log: Names and IDs fixed; the CIDR still overlaps.

choices.feedback: The mesh connects, but Pod IPs can't be routed directly between overlapping CIDRs; failover will not work as planned.

choices.label: Connect them as they are and fix collisions if they show up

effects.log: The clusters are connected with colliding IDs.

choices.feedback: With the same cluster ID, identities from both clusters collide; policy starts allowing and denying the wrong Pods.

globalPrompt.title: Make checkout fail over
globalPrompt.context: Each cluster's checkout Service only load-balances to its own Pods.

choices.label: Annotate checkout with service.cilium.io/global: "true" in both clusters, same name and namespace, and test by scaling east's checkout to zero

effects.log: Checkout is global; with east at zero, traffic goes to west.

choices.feedback: A global service with the same name and namespace in each cluster load-balances across both; the test proves failover.

choices.label: Annotate it in east only
choices.feedback: Both clusters must declare the Service global; one side alone does not give you two-way failover.

choices.label: Skip the annotation and plan to switch external DNS by hand during an outage

effects.log: Failover stays a manual DNS change.

choices.feedback: The mesh is unused; an outage again waits for someone to change DNS and for caches to expire.

affPrompt.title: Cross-region latency
affPrompt.context: A global service balances across both clusters by default, so half the calls cross regions and database writes slow down.

choices.label: Set service.cilium.io/affinity: "local" so each cluster prefers its own checkout Pods and uses the other's only when it has none

effects.log: Calls stay local; remote Pods take over only when local ones are gone.

choices.feedback: Local affinity keeps traffic in-region while keeping the remote cluster as failover.

choices.label: Accept the cross-region traffic as the price of failover
choices.feedback: Failover works, but every customer pays the latency.

choices.label: Remove the global annotation from west so east keeps its traffic local

effects.log: West's Service is no longer global.

choices.feedback: That removes west from failover: east's outage would be a full outage again.

reflection.question: Write the change record: what had to change before the clusters could connect, and how checkout now fails over without crossing regions in normal running.

scoring.modelReasoning: Cluster Mesh joins clusters into one connectivity and identity domain, so each needs a unique name and ID, and Pod IPs can only be routed between non-overlapping Pod CIDRs. A Service with the same name and namespace annotated service.cilium.io/global in each cluster load-balances across all of them; test failover by removing local endpoints. Affinity tunes that: local prefers the cluster's own endpoints and falls back to remote ones only when none are left.
